record.scientificName: Convolvulus meonanthus Hoffmanns. & Link, Fl. Portug. 1: 369, t. 69. 1820. (Hoffmannsegg and Link 1813
record.authorship: Hoffmanns. & Link, Fl. Portug. 1: 369, t. 69. 1820. (Hoffmannsegg and Link 1813

descriptions.description: Description. Annual herb, commonly branched at the base, reaching c. 40 cm, stems and leaves with long, stiff spreading hairs. Basal leaves 2.5 - 4.5 x 0.7 - 1 cm, obovate-spathulate, obtuse, entire, base attenuate into a pseudopetiole, stem leaves 1.5 - 5.5 x 0.2 - 1 (- 1.8) cm, oblong or lanceolate, sessile. Flowers solitary, axillary, pedunculate; bracts lanceolate, acute; peduncles 1.5 - 5 cm, slender, flexuose, becoming recurved in fruit; bracteoles 0.5 mm, triangular, acute; pedicels 2 - 4 mm, not well differentiated from the peduncles; sepals 5 - 6 x 2 - 2.5 mm, ovate, acute to apiculate, margin, scarious, ciliate or glabrous, sepals otherwise more or less glabrous; corolla 1.5 - 2.4 cm long, tricoloured blue, white and yellow, weakly 5 - angled with apices of lobes pointed, midpetaline bands adpressed pilose; ovary glabrous; style glabrous, divided c. 5 mm above base, stigmas 2.5 - 3 mm. Capsule glabrous, much exceeding calyx; seeds tuberculate. [Sa'ad 1967: 185; Pignatti 1982: 388; Silvestre 2012: 268, 271 (plate)]
Distribution. West Mediterranean region, perhaps only in Europe: Algeria (?); Morocco (?); Portugal (Brummitt & Ernst 5985); Spain (Boissier & Reuter 1841, Todaro 922); Italy (Woolley-Dod 1756).
